clue.text: Boast of famous friend? Pardon me, that's bad

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters of the apology are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for a crass boast about knowing a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: To namedrop is to mention celebrities casually as if they were acquaintances, a form of showing off.

clue.text: Stop, being lame

definitions.meaning: limping, an old sense still seen in the adjective for walking with a limp

explanation.surface: A command to stop, given because someone is limping.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means cease moving; as an archaic adjective it means crippled or limping.

clue.text: Festival with two unknowns but a lot of stars

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
in algebra x and y are the usual unknowns
in algebra x and y are the usual unknowns

explanation.surface: A festival with two mystery guests yet plenty of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' tempts toward celebrities at the gala, but the definition is astronomical.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of stars bound by gravity.

clue.text: Don't stand for what church robber may do?

definitions.meaning: a thief in church might steal one of the benches

explanation.surface: An invitation to sit, playfully linked to a thief in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sit down; literally it describes stealing a church bench.

clue.text: But it may be tall tale

definitions.text: But it may be tall tale

parts.words: But it may be tall tale
parts.note: a tall tale is an exaggerated yarn, yet the clue plays on tall versus its opposite to describe a brief piece of fiction

explanation.surface: A remark about exaggerated yarns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tall' suggests height, but the opposite word combines with a literary form to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief work of prose fiction may well be an exaggerated, tall story.

clue.text: Emperor is usurper, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for a grabber of power is said aloud

parts.note: one who seizes power is a seizer

explanation.surface: A claim that a Roman ruler gained the throne illegitimately.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar's name became the title for Roman rulers, so it is a byword for an imperial ruler.

clue.text: Shell of vehicle quickly assembled

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: The body of a car being put together at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell of vehicle' reads as a car body, but 'Shell' alone is the definition; 'of' and 'assembled' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper casing of a tortoise or crab.

clue.text: Delighted boy comes round after time

indicators.note: comes round says the name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward
something late comes after the expected time

explanation.surface: A thrilled lad turns up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' wants to be T, but 'after time' together gives LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated is a synonym of overjoyed or thrilled.

clue.text: Religious leader enters a sham Indian heritage

indicators.note: enters says the letter goes inside the following words

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Religious

explanation.surface: A fraudulent guru moves into a phoney retreat in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious leader' looks like a guru, but it is just the letter R placed inside A SHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a secluded religious community or retreat in India.

clue.text: Advanced fast

definitions.meaning: the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone moved ahead quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as quick but is the season of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Money advanced is loaned; the forty days of fasting before Easter carry the same name.

clue.text: The samurai in conflict, so unprofessional

indicators.note: letters in conflict are at odds and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Warriors fighting badly, showing lack of skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conflict' rearranges THESAMURAI; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish means inexpert, like work by a beginner.

clue.text: After homework, always make an advance

indicators.note: After places the homework word ahead of the word for always

parts.note: prep is school homework in British boarding schools
ay (or aye) is a poetic word for ever

explanation.surface: Once schoolwork is done, someone always lends money.
explanation.walkthrough: PREP is British school slang for homework.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepay is to settle a bill before receiving goods, paying up front.

clue.text: Detective magazine?

explanation.surface: Asking about a crime periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a long-running British satirical fortnightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired investigator is called this; it is also the name of a well-known British satirical magazine.

clue.text: Trade fair certain to get publicity

parts.note: an expo is a trade exhibition
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A trade show guaranteed to attract media coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure means public attention or media coverage.

clue.text: Cleric of uncertain stripe

indicators.note: letters of uncertain arrangement are unsettled and can be reordered

explanation.surface: A clergyman of doubtful allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripe' here means kind or type, but its letters are rearranged; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister of religion.

clue.text: Closely watching boys' activity in uniform

definitions.meaning: the youth movement founded by Baden-Powell, with badges and uniforms

explanation.surface: Observing lads dressed in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnoitring means surveying closely; the uniformed youth movement is named for the same activity.

clue.text: Grabbed by boys, warrant officer faints

indicators.note: Grabbed by says the officer is held within the word for boys

parts.note: sons are boys
WO is the military abbreviation for warrant officer

explanation.surface: An officer collapses after being seized by youths.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to pass out or keel over.

clue.text: Individual performers thus love to be seen in catalogues

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: to be seen in places the zero for love inside the catalogues word

parts.note: lists are catalogues
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Solo artists who adore appearing in brochures.
explanation.definitionFit: Soloists perform alone rather than as part of an ensemble.

clue.text: One lays out cards in patterns

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a dealer deals cards

explanation.surface: Someone dealing a hand in a set arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patterns' means models of perfection, not designs; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards or exemplars to be imitated.

clue.text: Intensely suspicious-soldier has no identification

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

explanation.surface: A distrustful soldier lacks papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranoid describes someone excessively mistrustful of others.

clue.text: In war, a blessing to have land for crops

indicators.note: In says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: During wartime, farmland is a godsend.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable describes ground suitable for ploughing and growing grain.

clue.text: Insect-guess its behaviour?

definitions.meaning: a guess about what it does: perhaps it takes to the air

explanation.surface: Speculating on how a bug acts.
explanation.definitionFit: The ephemeral winged insect's name also reads as a guess that it might take wing.

clue.text: Mule is sick of cereal

indicators.note: sick letters are out of sorts and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A donkey has had enough of its breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick of' reads as fed up with; 'sick' rearranges MULEIS and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: Be successful in getting something built

definitions.meaning: to be assured of success in life
having an item constructed for you

explanation.surface: Thriving by commissioning construction.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be assured of prosperity; literally it means to have had an item constructed.

clue.text: Bad weather managed to keep one in

indicators.note: to keep says the word for managed holds the numeral

parts.note: ran means managed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Coping with storms by staying indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain, a downpour, is the classic sort of bad weather.

clue.text: Stock car competition

explanation.surface: A stock car event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock car' looks like a single phrase, but it splits between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Race means ancestry or breed, and also a speed contest between cars.

clue.text: Be dismissed, but keep batting?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to deflect the ball onto your own wicket and be out

explanation.surface: A cricketer out, yet carrying on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, playing on means hitting the ball onto your own stumps, which gets you out.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket phrase means being bowled off your own bat; generally it means continue the game.

clue.text: Alas, rejected Sodom, say, for lecherousness

indicators.note: rejected means the word Alas is turned back

parts.note: Sodom is an example of a biblical city

explanation.surface: Sodom was spurned for its lewdness.
explanation.definitionFit: Salacity means lewdness or indecent lust.
